suppress.notes: netty-transport 4.2.15.Final. Accepted because no STABLE upgrade exists: the next published release of io.netty is 5.0.0.Alpha2 (Maven Central, checked 2026-08-08), and a major-version alpha is not an acceptable dependency for the money path. Not assessed individually for reachability; re-check for a stable 4.2.x or 5.x GA at expiry.

kotlin-stdlib 2.3.21. Accepted because no STABLE upgrade exists: the next published release of org.jetbrains.kotlin is 2.4.20-Beta2 (Maven Central, checked 2026-08-08). Reached here via a `cpe:2.3:a:jetbrains:kotlin` mapping — a product-level CPE for a language distribution matched against a stdlib jar — which is the classic over-match shape, but that is context and not the justification. Re-check for a stable 2.4.x at expiry.

opentelemetry-semconv 1.41.1. This one is NOT "no upgrade exists" — 1.43.0 is published. It is accepted because the artefact arrives transitively and is managed by no Spring Boot version property, so pinning it means adding a dependencyManagement entry that overrides what the OpenTelemetry BOM resolved, and there is no evidence the bump clears the finding: the match is via `cpe:2.3:a:opentelemetry:opentelemetry`, a product-level CPE applied to a jar that contains only generated semantic-convention constants. Bumping to satisfy a name-based match, without first establishing that the CVE applies, is a change made to a scanner rather than to a risk. OWED AT EXPIRY: establish whether CVE-2026-39883 applies to this artefact at all, then either pin 1.43.0+ or replace this entry with a reasoned permanent one.

android-json 0.0.20131108.vaadin1, TEST SCOPE ONLY (transitive via spring-boot-starter-test → json-path). Two independent reasons, either sufficient: (a) it is never packaged into the image, so it cannot be reached by any deployed code path; (b) CVE-2008-0986 is a 2008 vulnerability in the GOOGLE ANDROID SDK, reached here through `cpe:2.3:a:google:android_sdk`, matched to a repackaged JSON parser Vaadin vendored. A product-level CPE for a mobile SDK applied to a JSON jar is a name collision, not a finding. Longer expiry than the netty entries because reason (a) does not depend on any release.

httpcore5 5.0.2, TEST SCOPE ONLY. It is not a declared dependency at all — it is a POM embedded inside docker-java-transport-zerodep-3.4.1.jar, which Testcontainers uses to talk to the Docker daemon during the integration suite. It is never packaged into the image and never runs outside a CI runner or a developer laptop. The version cannot be bumped from this pom either: it is shaded inside another artifact, so the fix is a Testcontainers upgrade, not a dependencyManagement entry. Re-check when the testcontainers BOM moves past 1.20.5.

netty-transport 4.2.15.Final, the remaining two. Same reason as the block above: no stable upgrade exists (next release is 5.0.0.Alpha2, Maven Central 2026-08-08).
WORTH RECORDING because it is confusing: the report prints these as CVE-2026-59898(6.3) and CVE-2026-59899(6.9), BOTH BELOW the failBuildOnCVSS threshold of 7.0 — and they still failed the build. The printed figure is not the figure the gate compares. Dependency-Check falls back to another score (CVSS v2, or the highest available across scoring systems) when deciding, so "the number shown is under the threshold" is not a safe reason to leave something unsuppressed. The first round left these two out on exactly that reasoning and the build stayed red.

tomcat-embed-core 11.0.24. The bump from 11.0.22 to 11.0.24 cleared FIVE of the six findings against this artefact — CVE-2026-55276, CVE-2026-53434, CVE-2026-59083, CVE-2026-59084 and CVE-2026-53404 are gone, which is the upgrade doing real work rather than a version number moving. CVE-2026-66299 survives it, and 11.0.24 is the current release (Maven Central, 2026-08-08), so there is nothing further to upgrade to. Re-check at expiry: Tomcat patches often, and this is the entry most likely to be removable rather than renewed.
